gaps.sentence: Unlike some politicians, she ___ her promises.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'promises' (she is unlike other politicians)
gaps.explanation: keep a promise means to do what you promised; the contrast with other politicians shows the positive verb.

gaps.sentence: The ___ traffic added an hour to our journey.
gaps.explanation: heavy traffic means a lot of vehicles on the road; 'thick traffic' is not standard.

gaps.sentence: You are ___ a big risk if you invest all your money in one company.
gaps.explanation: take a risk means to do something that might have a bad result.

gaps.sentence: The children were told not to ___ so much noise.
gaps.explanation: make a noise / make noise is the fixed collocation.

gaps.sentence: It was three in the morning, but I was wide ___.
gaps.explanation: wide awake means completely awake; it is the fixed collocation with 'wide'.

gaps.sentence: The manager ___ an announcement about the changes yesterday.
gaps.explanation: make an announcement is the fixed collocation for stating something publicly.

gaps.sentence: She ___ no difficulty finding the address.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ no difficulty doing something
gaps.explanation: have no difficulty (in) doing something is the fixed pattern; 'made no difficulty' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a fortune selling software online.
gaps.explanation: make a fortune means to earn a very large amount of money.
